To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
culture is being used in South Korean multicultural policy as a tool to manage diversity and to maintain existing inequalities.

(a) the language of culture has been used to construct female marriage migrants as a social problem and to divert attention from structural inequalities; (b) the discourse of cultural deficiency has been used to justify the need for multicultural policies; and (c) the proposed policy shift from multiculturalism to cultural diversity is problematic as it does not challenge the dominant discourse of cultural deficiency and does not address issues of power and inequalities.

(a) culture has been employed as a tool of social control to manage diversity; (b) culture has been deployed to divert attention away from structural issues of power and inequality; and (c) the language of culture has become the primary means of constructing migrants as cultural others and of defining the boundaries of national belonging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
interrogating the uses of cultural discourses, and the politics of culture in the making of social policies.

interrogating the uses of the concept of culture in the construction and resolution of social problems in multicultural societies, and in the process, to contribute towards developing a critical multiculturalism.
the question of whether the politics of diversity can be re-imagined and re-articulated in ways that can contribute to a more just society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
culture is not simply a neutral concept, but a contested and political category that is used in a strategic way to justify certain political agendas.
the politics of diversity is a site where the cultural politics of difference are played out, and the language of culture can be deployed as a means to reify and naturalise social inequalities.
multiculturalism in South Korea is a political strategy that seeks to reassert the nation's cultural homogeneity by constructing the 'cultural other' as a problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the article demonstrates that culture is a key concept that has been deployed in the politics of multiculturalism, and the language of culture can be used in both positive and negative ways.

the discourse of cultural diversity in the politics of multiculturalism in South Korea has not been able to escape from the essentialist and deficit-oriented logic of the discourse of cultural difference and cultural deficiency.
culture has become a powerful tool for both the construction of difference and the production of inequality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

culture is a highly contested and fluid concept, and its deployment in the politics of multiculturalism is often used to obscure the underlying power dynamics and structural inequalities that shape the lives of minority groups.
the culturalisation of diversity is not simply an innocent attempt to address social problems.

the politics of diversity in South Korea is not only a matter of inclusion and exclusion, but also a process of cultural production that involves the construction and negotiation of cultural meanings, and a struggle over power relations and social hierarchies.
